dimensions.gloss: How much of the output the AI produced relative to the human, expressed as an ordered scale from none/minimal involvement to full AI generation.
variants: specify the level of ai assistance
the degree of human involvement in its production
the level of ai involvement in research and writing
dimensions.note: task-related ai ownership is a close call: it frames the scale as ownership levels (no/low-delegated/partial/shared/high-human) rather than 'AI involvement', but it is the same ordinal axis.

dimensions.gloss: A named categorical taxonomy of the role or agency level an AI system played (e.g. Scribe, Executor, Evaluator, Co-ideator, Promptee; or a tiered autonomy hierarchy), ranked by kind of AI agency rather than by amount.
dimensions.note: 'scribe' is one value drawn from the AI role taxonomy itself; included here as a close call rather than as its own axis.

dimensions.canonical_label: Disclosure location / scope within the work
dimensions.gloss: Which part or section of a document or work (whole manuscript, specific sections, specific tasks) the AI-use disclosure refers to or must appear in.
Whether, and under what boundaries or approved-source restrictions, AI use is permitted, prohibited, or left unaddressed.
variants: speciﬁcation of permissible uses of ai
dimensions.note: close call: 'scope clarity' comes from a clinical AI capability-boundary context rather than an authorship-permission policy, but it records the same 'what AI is or isn't allowed to do' axis.

dimensions.gloss: Which named AI tool or model (e.g. ChatGPT, Grammarly, Claude) was used.
variants: the name of ai tool(s) used

dimensions.canonical_label: Model technical details and generation parameters
dimensions.gloss: Whether technical details of the AI model and its generation settings (parameters, stochasticity controls, prompt-attempt counts, output selection) must be declared.
variants: specific technical details of the ai model used should be declared

dimensions.gloss: Whether the exact prompts given to an AI system must be reported as part of disclosure.
variants: specific prompts used should be reported

dimensions.canonical_label: Task or purpose of AI use
dimensions.gloss: The specific task, purpose, or job (writing, editing, translation, coding, summarizing) that AI was used for.
variants: specific course tasks or assignment associated with ai-use
specific uses of genai in writing assistance
the five most frequently mentioned task categories

dimensions.gloss: A tiered classification of AI use by how severe, high-stakes, or epistemically sensitive it is, used to set the required level of oversight and disclosure.
variants: severity and reversibility of potential harm
the appropriate level of oversight and disclosure

dimensions.gloss: The particular task or contribution (e.g. supplying samples, data analysis, visualization, domain selection) attributed to a human or AI contributor in the work.
variants: the evolving role of human researchers
dimensions.note: close call: 'soldier' and 'sample manipulation' are individual role/task labels from source tables rather than named axes, but they describe the same 'who did what specific task' axis as the others.

dimensions.gloss: The threshold of contribution (conception/design, intellectual content, interpretation) that qualifies a contributor for authorship.
variants: the intellectual content, interpretation, argument, or presentation of a manuscript

dimensions.gloss: A fixed bundle of specific data points (tool name/version, operator identity, dates, predictions, biases, etc.) that a disclosure statement or record must include to be considered complete.
variants: the minimum information necessary to understand

dimensions.gloss: Technical fields (digital signature, encryption technique, version, hashing algorithm) attached to a claim to allow authenticity verification.
The category of technical mechanism (cryptographic attestation, detection tooling, log/blockchain/ontology-based systems) used to establish or verify content provenance and authenticity.
dimensions.note: 'technical support' is a close call: it names a policy dimension (building detection/monitoring tools) rather than classifying an existing technology, but it concerns the same class of technical provenance/detection mechanisms.

dimensions.gloss: The named type of relationship (cites, supports, contradicts, derived-from, connects-to-subject) linking one piece of content or claim to another in a provenance graph.
What material the content or record is built from and where it originated, including attribution and institutional origin.
Whether the basis for an AI system's output, or the system's inner workings, is visible to users and reviewers.
dimensions.note: close call: one label is about visibility of the basis for a recommendation, the other about general AI-system transparency in a checklist; grouped as the same internal-transparency axis, distinct from disclosure-of-use.

dimensions.canonical_label: Layers of a technical trust/provenance framework
dimensions.gloss: Named layers within a multi-layer technical scheme (e.g. similarity-and-history checking, provenance, identity, authentication, authority, factual truth) that together assess content trustworthiness.
dimensions.note: close call: grouped because both are literal 'layer' components of a layered classification scheme, even though the surrounding schemes differ.

dimensions.gloss: When contributions occurred, and whether the analysis supports bounded, reproducible, time-anchored review.
Whether the underlying source code is accessible, licensed as open source, and/or modifiable.
Protections and controls described against data breaches, cyberattacks, or other security vulnerabilities.
Rules governing what data (secondary or sensitive) may be entered into an AI system, such as blanket or tiered bans.
Whether and where a study's registration or protocol (trial number, PROSPERO/OSF number, protocol version) is disclosed.
The type and quality of the link between a published dataset and the paper it accompanies.
The categories of actors or stakeholders (builders, creators, distributors, authors, journals, participants, readers) who have an interest in or connection to the work.
A categorical classification of content by its degree of AI origin, such as original/augmented/synthetic text, or a bright-line threshold between reactive augmentation and generative synthesis.
dimensions.note: close call: one scheme uses three text-typology categories, the other a binary threshold, but both classify content by type/degree of AI origin rather than a continuous extent scale.

dimensions.gloss: Whether a contribution was specific and non-substitutable, i.e. whether a different prompter/contributor could have produced an equivalent result.
Whether and how significant errors, malfunctions, or the AI system's error rate were defined, identified, and reported.
Whether researchers align their analysis methodologies and incorporate AI-specific reflexive practice into their work.
Rubric criteria used to grade the quality of AI-assisted student work, such as accuracy/rigor, critical evaluation of AI output, and testing an answer against real context.
variants: test the answer against patient context

dimensions.gloss: Named strategies for redesigning academic assessment tasks in response to AI availability, such as scenario-based tasks or combining secure exams with AI-enabled coursework.
variants: secure high-stakes exams combined with ai-enabled coursework

dimensions.gloss: Generic quality-assurance-framework elements (alongside Intellectual Quality) retained or extended when adapting a framework for AI-related assessment.
Named dimensions (terminal objective, support persistence) used to classify an AI-mediated instructional arrangement.

dimensions.canonical_label: Workflow stage as basis for disclosure
dimensions.gloss: Disclosure requirements organized around, or a workflow expressed as, sequential stages of content production (creation, provenance capture, review, authenticity checking, disclosure, external assurance).
Named layers (storycraft, engagement levers, AI workflow) of a content-production framework describing how a piece is crafted, rather than how its AI use is disclosed.
dimensions.note: close call: these describe production-process layers rather than disclosure content, grouped together because they are parallel labeled layers (A/B/D) of one scheme.

dimensions.gloss: Basic identifying metadata fields for a piece of software: its name and its description/abstract.
Whether and how paid or sponsored content (endorsements, affiliate marketing, native advertising) is clearly labeled as such.
Categories of service, teaching, or technical-competency contribution that count toward credit for promoting open data/software practices.
variants: service as part of professional organizations, groups, journals, or committees that support and promote open practices for data and software
teaching, training, outreach, and other community activities to advance best practices in open data and open-source software
technical competency in the creation, management, and use of data and/or software

dimensions.gloss: A tracking identifier assigned to a specific run/execution, used to reference it elsewhere.
Protective mechanisms recorded for the reviewer or author side of a disclosure policy, e.g. penalty protection, interpretive guidance, appeal mechanisms.
An editorial concern that AI use in research risks reinforcing incremental work at the expense of breakthrough research.
A methodology-reporting item recording the size of the sample used in a study.
One of a set of named literacies students need, concerning recognition of scholarly authority, within an AI-literacy framework.
The set of topics (definitions of misconduct, detection-software use, assessment redesign) a policy document's scope section covers.
Documentation of literature/database search strategies used and whether they were saved or exported.
The literal title/heading given to the section of a document where AI-use disclosure is placed.
The industry or sector (e.g. financial services, government/high-assurance) a scheme's guidance is profiled for.
Whether a human's act of selecting among AI-generated options counts as a criterion for judging the nature of their contribution.
Whether publication of cost-effectiveness sensitivity-analysis results is mandatory, recommended, or not required.
variants: sensitivity analysis results for the cost-effectiveness analysis

dimensions.gloss: Contextual disclosure factors around a publication: where it is located (journal, supplement, online), its relationship to other publications, and the researcher's perspective or commercial/legal context.
The name of a specific open disclosure specification built from seven sections, referenced as a whole rather than as a single axis.
A breakdown of metadata into several named classes, such as operational data, project/proposal information, or data ownership.
Whether a disclosure's visual presentation (e.g. text size) is smaller than, equal to, or larger than surrounding content.
Concerns raised about bias, sensitivity, and privacy when the work represents people.
Which other named guideline (e.g. ICMJE, COPE, WAME) a scheme cites as its source or authority.
One named element of policy content concerning which specific criteria trigger a disclosure requirement.
The degree to which a policy's requirements are clearly specified versus left vague.
Contextual information about the spoken language recorded for language datasets.
How much control stakeholders have in a repository's or resource's governance, rated on a none-to-full scale.

dimensions.canonical_label: Standards concerning AI applications as authors
dimensions.gloss: General editorial standards declaring that AI applications cannot be authors and must be described in Methods/Acknowledgments.
The validity/trust state (valid, trusted, well-formed, unknown) assigned to a manifest after integrity checks.
The legally defined categories of misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, improper authorship, improper ownership, security breaches) that generative AI use may implicate.
The levels (individual, tooling, governance) across which distinct failure modes are classified.
A named dimension concerning how much agency and bounded choice a student retains when using AI.
The stance a student is classified as taking toward AI-use disclosure, ranging from potential violator to responsible discloser to reflective practitioner.
A named thematic section of a checklist/questionnaire concerning study design, alongside research team, participant interaction, data practices, and data analysis.
A student's psychological awareness of AI threatening their sense of professional identity or value.
A named taxonomy of research/scholarly activity types, such as community-building or teaching-and-learning.
The specific terms (training set, validation set, test set, instance) used for data partitions, and their definitions.
The models and metrics a dataset has been tested against using a machine-learning approach.
Top-level categories of a coding frame used to study how advertising and editorial content are integrated (ad functions, staff roles, publisher control, terms of service).
The process adopted to resolve disputes over authorship.
variants: the conflict resolution processes adopted to handle authorship disputes

dimensions.gloss: Key information about the data an algorithm was trained on, including its source, scope, quality, and inner correlations.
variants: the data on which the algorithm was trained

dimensions.gloss: The three overarching dimensions (integrity, equity, pedagogy) an assessment-design framework is structured around.
variants: the dimensions of integrity, equity, and pedagogy

dimensions.gloss: An editorial point about how scientists' roles must evolve (intuition, ethical judgment, long-term thinking) as AI becomes embedded in research.
A bundled disclosure item naming the languages involved, verification processes used, and data governance protocols applied.

dimensions.canonical_label: Extent of human review and verification
dimensions.gloss: How much human review and verification was applied to AI-generated output.
variants: the extent of human review and verification

dimensions.gloss: The stage of the marketing cycle (research, strategy formulation, marketing-mix actions) at which AI or a disclosed activity was applied.
Whether the results obtained support the AI system's intended use in its deployment setting.
